input:
Here's an interview question that I use to evaluate product managers. What would a good answer be?
\*\*\*Start of question\*\*\*

Preamble

- This is a case study / role play question.
- Feel free to ask me any question
- There are no tricks / gotchas
- The simplest answer is probably the best. This is the biggest mistake people make. No need to be fancy, keep it as simple as possible.

The setup

- You are the PM of the ETA team at Uber.
 - ETA is estimated time of arrival — the number that says how far your car is
 - ETA important because not only does it tell the customer how far the car is, but it is an input into all kinds of pricing / supply planning things. So if it goes down or has issues, it’s a big deal.
 - The ETA score is generated by a service which you are the PM of. You do normal stuff like try to make it better over time and ensure it’s not broken.
- One day the customer success team comes to you
 - They say, “hey we just realized we never told you about this data set that we have”
 - The data set is a log of all complaints submitted by users to Uber \*\*\*\*through the app.
 - E.g. “driver was rude”, “car didn’t show up”, “i got charged twice”
 - Each complaint is one row in the data set.
 - Each complaint is tagged with a category. e.g. `driver related`, `price related`, `ETA related`
 
 
 📌 For the candidate to discover through questions:
 
 - The data is always up to date in real-time (keeping it simple)
 - There is no open text field. The columns are just `trip\_id, time, category`
 - The data goes back historically for years
 
 
 

- You have have had outage issues with the ETA system in the past and you think this data may be an opportunity to detect when there are outages.
- The question to answer is: how can you use this data to detect outages? We want to be able to automatically wake up an engineer in the middle of the night if we detect an outage.
📌 For the candidate to clarify through questions:

- We’re not interested in fixing the issue or in root cause analysis
- We can assume there’s a working alerting system e.g. Pagerduty
- We don’t want to use any other data sources, just the ticket data

\*\*\*End of Question\*\*\*
simple:
Here is a problem I use to see how well someone can think about products. What would be a good way to solve it?

***Start of problem***

Background

- This is a situation where you pretend to be someone at work.
- You can ask me anything you need to know.
- There aren’t any hidden tricks.
- The easiest answer is usually the best one. Don’t try to make it too complicated, just keep it simple.

The situation

- Imagine you are in charge of the team at Uber that works on ETAs.
 - ETA means estimated time of arrival — it’s the number that shows how far away your ride is.
 - ETAs are important because they tell customers when their ride will arrive, and they also help Uber decide on prices and plan how many cars are needed. If the ETA isn’t right, it can cause problems.
 - Your team is responsible for the service that creates the ETA. You work on making it better and making sure it doesn’t break.
- One day, the team that helps customers tells you something new.
 - They say, “We just realized we never told you about some information we have.”
 - This information is a record of all the complaints people send to Uber through the app.
 - For example, complaints like “the driver was rude,” “the car didn’t come,” or “I was charged the wrong amount.”
 - Each complaint is one line in the record.
 - Each complaint is also labeled with what it’s about, like `driver issues`, `price issues`, or `ETA issues`.

Important things to find out by asking questions:

- The information is always new and up-to-date.
- There isn’t a place for people to write long explanations. The record just has `trip number, time, and category`.
- The record goes back many years.

- Your ETA system has had problems in the past, and you think this information might help you find when those problems happen again.
- The problem to solve is: how can you use this information to find when the ETA system is having problems? We want to be able to automatically alert an engineer if we find a problem, even in the middle of the night.

Things to ask me to make sure you understand:

- We don’t need to fix the problem or figure out why it happened.
- We can assume you have a system to send alerts, like Pagerduty.
- We only want to use this information about complaints, not any other information.

***End of Problem***
friendly:
I came across this interview question for product managers and was wondering what a strong response might look like.

***Start of question***

Background

- This is a scenario-based question.
- You are welcome to ask me anything you need to know.
- There aren’t any hidden complexities.
- The most straightforward solution is usually the best one. Many people overcomplicate things unnecessarily, so simplicity is key.

The Situation

- Imagine you are the product manager for the ETA team at Uber.
 - ETA, or estimated time of arrival, is the number displayed to customers indicating how far away their ride is.
 - Accurate ETA is crucial, as it influences both customer experience and internal processes like pricing and resource allocation. Any problems with it are significant.
 - You manage the service that generates the ETA score, working to improve its accuracy and reliability.
- One day, the customer support team informs you
 - They mention they never previously shared a particular dataset with you.
 - This dataset is a record of all user complaints submitted via the Uber app.
 - For example, complaints might include issues like “driver behavior,” “no-show vehicle,” or “duplicate charges.”
 - Each complaint is a single entry in the dataset.
 - Each complaint is categorized (e.g., `driver issue`, `pricing issue`, `ETA issue`).

Important points for the person answering:

- The data is continuously updated in real-time.
- The dataset only contains structured data: `trip ID`, `timestamp`, and `category`. There is no free-text field.
- Historical data is available for several years.

- You've previously experienced outages with the ETA system and believe this data could help identify them.
- The task is to determine how to use this data to detect outages, with the goal of automatically alerting an engineer if an outage is detected.
Clarifications for the person answering:

- We're focused on outage *detection*, not on resolving the underlying issues or conducting root cause analysis.
- Assume a functional alerting system, such as PagerDuty, is already in place.
- Limit your solution to this ticket data; do not incorporate other data sources.

***End of Question***
academic:
Here is a case study designed to assess the skills of product managers. Consider the following scenario and formulate your approach.

Background:

- This is a simulated, practical exercise.
- You are encouraged to ask clarifying questions.
- The exercise is straightforward; avoid unnecessary complexity. Simplicity is often the most effective solution.

Scenario:

You are the product manager responsible for the Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) service at Uber. The ETA represents the predicted arrival time for a rider’s vehicle and is a critical input for pricing and logistical planning. This ETA is calculated by a service under your management, where you focus on its ongoing improvement and reliability.

Recently, the customer support team informed you about a previously unknown data source: a record of all user-submitted complaints lodged through the Uber application. Each complaint is recorded as a single entry, categorized by the nature of the issue (e.g., driver behavior, charges, or ETA accuracy). The dataset includes the trip identifier, the time of submission, and the complaint category. This data is continuously updated and spans several years of historical records.

Given past instances of service disruptions with the ETA system, you believe this complaint data could potentially be used to proactively identify new outages. 

The objective is to determine how this data can be leveraged to automatically alert an engineer on call when an outage is detected. 

For the purposes of this exercise, focus on outage detection only – root cause analysis or issue resolution are not required. Assume a functional alerting system, such as PagerDuty, is already in place and that you should not incorporate any additional data sources beyond the complaint data.
